key_facts: patient has a history of chronic pulmonary coccidiomycosis
patient was being treated with fluconazole
pembrolizumab treatment was stopped 3 months prior due to a morbilliform reaction
new skin eruption appeared different from previous reaction
blood culture results showed no growth at 1 week
serum β-D-glucan, galactomannan, Coccidioides antibody, and immunodiffusion results were negative

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including fever, hypotension, and a new widespread skin eruption, along with laboratory findings such as a low white blood cell count, anemia, and thrombocytopenia, are consistent with a diagnosis of intravascular large B-cell lymphoma. The skin biopsy findings showing intravascular atypical cells further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Intravascular NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and biopsy findings do not specifically suggest NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type, which typically involves the nasal area and has distinct immunophenotypic features.

rejected.label: Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm
rejected.why: This diagnosis is less likely given the patient's clinical presentation and the lack of specific findings suggestive of this rare and aggressive neoplasm.

rejected.label: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The patient's skin biopsy did not show the characteristic large cell morphology with CD30 positivity typical of anaplastic large cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma
rejected.why: The patient's clinical presentation, laboratory findings, and biopsy results do not align with adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma, which is typically associated with HTLV-1 infection and has distinct clinical and immunophenotypic features.
